summary: This case study details the technical implementation and debugging of SuperDimmer, a macOS screen dimming utility that uses non-opaque NSWindow overlays with hybrid z-ordering and CGSetDisplayTransferByTable for gamma-based color temperature adjustment. It provides concrete, hard-earned solutions to complex AppKit memory management and window-ordering issues.
strengths: Provides real-world, actionable solutions to subtle AppKit crash bugs (e.g., EXC_BAD_ACCESS in objc_release on window deinit).
Clearly explains the architectural tradeoffs between window overlays, gamma LUTs, and DDC/CI.
Backed by a robust supporting repository containing comprehensive debugging guides and active commit history.
Well-documented code snippets illustrating hybrid z-ordering and safe overlay hiding patterns.
weaknesses: The scope is highly platform-specific to macOS, limiting generalizability to other operating systems.
Some discussions on performance overhead and timing delays (e.g., 0.5s Space change delay) are empirical rather than grounded in formal benchmarking.
suggestions: Expand the discussion on how window-ordering behaves under heavily loaded Spaces or Mission Control animations.
Include a brief architectural diagram comparing the lifecycle of safeHideOverlay versus standard NSWindow.close().

claims.text: CGSetDisplayTransferByTable allows setting 256-entry gamma lookup tables on macOS displays.
NSWindow.Level.floating and order(_:relativeTo:) can be combined to position custom windows above specific target windows.
CGSetDisplayTransferByFormula is an alternative CoreGraphics API for adjusting gamma correction parameters.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Background macOS Desktop Automation via Accessibility API: Patterns for AI Agents in Multi-Agent Environments
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on window compositor management, overlay UI lifecycles, and gamma transfer tables for visual dimming rather than accessibility-driven automation.
